items.title: Add explicit non-DONE/non-Authority/non-production disclaimer strings to milestone_status and milestone_closeout rendered output
items.context: packages/main/src/core/milestone-status.ts renderMilestoneStatusReport (~L1146-1187), the missing-ledger report, and the closeout report currently emit only 'Mode: read-only'. Add an explicit disclaimer line stating milestone progress is not lifecycle DONE, not Authority, not production readiness. Closes findings M6 (report lines re: M1.f/M6). Update packages/main/tests/milestone-status.test.mjs to assert the disclaimer string is present.
items.userSees:
After running `lattice milestone_status --storyId=<id>` (or the milestone_closeout report), the operator sees a new explicit disclaimer line directly under the existing `Mode: read-only` header of every rendered report. Concretely:

- `milestone_status` (populated ledger) header block now reads:
  `Milestone Status - <id>`
  `Mode: read-only`
  `Disclaimer: Milestone progress is not lifecycle DONE, not Authority-signed, and not production readiness.`
  `Phase: <phase>` ...

- `milestone_status` with a MISSING ledger prints the same `Disclaimer:` line under `Mode: read-only` (progress cannot be inferred, and the report still must not imply DONE/Authority/production).

- `milestone_closeout` snapshot report header now reads:
  `Milestone Closeout - <id>`
  `Mode: read-only historical snapshot`
  `Disclaimer: This is a historical milestone snapshot, not lifecycle DONE, not Authority-signed, and not production readiness.`

- `milestone_closeout` missing-snapshot report prints the same `Disclaimer:` line under `Mode: read-only historical snapshot`.

The disclaimer text is a stable literal that mentions all three negatives (not lifecycle DONE, not Authority, not production readiness). No table columns, ordering, or other lines change; it is purely an added advisory line, consistent with the read-only/no-write posture of these commands.

happy.desc: Logic (harness happy:0): buildMilestoneStatusReport with a populated ProofStory ledger, then renderMilestoneStatusReport. Split output on newlines; assert the line immediately AFTER 'Mode: read-only' is exactly the shared observability disclaimer 'Scope: observability only - reports milestone progress from the ProofStory ledger. This is NOT a lifecycle DONE, NOT an Authority verdict, and NOT a production-readiness gate.' and matches /observability only.*NOT a lifecycle DONE.*NOT an Authority verdict.*NOT a production-readiness gate/s. Delivered behavior emits the Scope-prefixed disclaimer, NOT a 'Disclaimer:' line.

Logic (harness happy:1): build a fully-completed report and buildMilestoneCloseoutSnapshot, then renderMilestoneCloseoutSnapshot. Assert the line immediately after 'Mode: read-only historical snapshot' equals the same shared MILESTONE_OBSERVABILITY_DISCLAIMER text (byte-identical to the status-path disclaimer), confirming the closeout-snapshot header carries the observability-scope disclaimer.

CLI (harness happy:2): run `lattice milestone_status --root <fixture> --storyId B-f7b3` against a story with a populated milestone-ledger.json. Pipe stdout through `awk '/^Mode: read-only$/{getline; print}'` and assert (grep -qxF) the captured line is exactly 'Scope: observability only - reports milestone progress from the ProofStory ledger. This is NOT a lifecycle DONE, NOT an Authority verdict, and NOT a production-readiness gate.'. Verifies the disclaimer end-to-end through the real CLI render, immediately under the read-only mode line.

edge.desc: Logic (harness edge:0): missing-ledger status path — buildMilestoneStatusReport with milestoneLedger:null, then renderMilestoneStatusReport. Assert output still contains the shared disclaimer (line right after 'Mode: read-only'), still shows 'Ledger: missing', and never claims completion (doesNotMatch /all ledger rows are completed/i). Confirms the read-only observability disclaimer is preserved when no ledger exists.

Logic (harness edge:1): missing-snapshot closeout path — renderMilestoneCloseoutMissingReport(report). Assert output preserves 'Snapshot: missing' and a 'Diagnostic:' line AND still carries the shared disclaimer as the line immediately after 'Mode: read-only historical snapshot'. Confirms the closeout-missing diagnostic render keeps the observability disclaimer.

Logic (harness edge:2): single-source structural property at the output level — grab the disclaimer line (line after the mode header) from all four render outputs (populated status, closeout snapshot, closeout-missing, missing-ledger status) and assert they are byte-identical (Set size 1) and equal the expected observability text. Proves the wording is single-sourced from one shared constant and cannot drift per path.

adversarial.desc: Adversarial CLI/grep guard (harness adversarial:0): against the REAL source packages/main/src/core/milestone-status.ts assert (a) `grep -cE "^const MILESTONE_OBSERVABILITY_DISCLAIMER ="` equals 1 (declared exactly once), and (b) for every source line matching /^\s*'Mode: read-only/ the NEXT source line is the MILESTONE_OBSERVABILITY_DISCLAIMER reference — so no read-only header can exist without the adjacent disclaimer guard. Genuinely adversarial: deleting any disclaimer reference (e.g. `sed 1187d`) makes the guard FAIL.

Adversarial negative-wording guard (harness adversarial:1): extract the disclaimer from the ACTUAL rendered status output. Assert it contains NO success-implying phrasing (doesNotMatch /\bproduction[- ]ready\b/i, /\bAuthority-signed\b/i, /\bis a lifecycle DONE\b/i) and that every risky token ('lifecycle DONE','Authority verdict','production-readiness gate') is negated by a nearby preceding NOT. Then mutate the line to 'This is a lifecycle DONE' and assert the guard THROWS — proving it is not pass-anything.

Adversarial mutation + full-suite regression (harness adversarial:2 plus `node --test packages/main/tests/milestone-status.test.mjs`): confirm the real render satisfies the disclaimer contract (observability only + all three NOT-negations), then drop a negation from the rendered text and assert the contract predicate REJECTS the mutant. Finally run the committed milestone-status suite and confirm all pre-existing assertions still pass (tests 1 / pass 1 / fail 0), guarding against regressions in the shared disclaimer wording.

items.title: Add 'Authority' to the milestone_status command-policy reason string to match milestone_closeout
items.context: packages/main/src/core/command-policy.ts: the milestone_status reason (~L237) omits Authority while milestone_closeout (~L238) includes it. Add the Authority-silence fix so both read-only commands disclaim Authority uniformly. Closes findings M6 Authority-silence note.
items.userSees: After the fix, an operator inspecting the command-policy reason for milestone_status (via `lattice help milestone_status`, `getCommandPolicy('milestone_status').reason`, or any surface that renders the policy reason) sees the disclaimer end with an explicit Authority disclaimer matching milestone_closeout. Concretely the milestone_status reason tail changes from "…advances no phase, and never claims automatic DONE or production readiness." to "…advances no phase, and never claims automatic DONE, production, or remote Authority readiness." Both read-only milestone commands (milestone_status and milestone_closeout) now literally contain the word "Authority" in their reason string, so a grep for the token no longer shows a gap. No behavior, phase-gating, ownershipClass, destructiveRisk, or allowedPhases changes — only the human-readable reason string gains the uniform Authority-silence disclaimer, closing the M6 Authority-silence note.

happy.desc: Build packages/main (npm --prefix packages/main run build) then run: node -e "const {getCommandPolicy}=require('./packages/main/dist/core/command-policy.js'); const r=getCommandPolicy('milestone_status').reason; if(!/Authority/.test(r)) throw new Error('milestone_status reason missing Authority: '+r); console.log('OK milestone_status discloses Authority');" — exits 0 and prints OK, proving the milestone_status reason now contains the Authority disclaimer.

Assert uniformity across both read-only milestone commands: node -e "const {getCommandPolicy}=require('./packages/main/dist/core/command-policy.js'); for(const c of ['milestone_status','milestone_closeout']){const r=getCommandPolicy(c).reason; if(!/Authority/.test(r)) throw new Error(c+' reason omits Authority');} console.log('both disclaim Authority');" — exits 0, confirming milestone_status now matches milestone_closeout's Authority-silence wording.

edge.desc: Confirm the change is reason-only and non-behavioral: node -e "const {getCommandPolicy}=require('./packages/main/dist/core/command-policy.js'); const p=getCommandPolicy('milestone_status'); if(p.status!=='supported'||p.ownershipClass!=='readOnly'||p.destructiveRisk!=='none'||p.allowedPhases!=='all') throw new Error('milestone_status policy fields drifted: '+JSON.stringify(p)); console.log('policy fields unchanged');" — exits 0, proving only the reason string changed and status/ownershipClass/destructiveRisk/allowedPhases are untouched.

Regression: run the existing milestone-status suite (npm --prefix packages/main run build && node packages/main/tests/milestone-status.test.mjs) and confirm it still exits 0, verifying the reason-string edit did not break the milestone_status/milestone_closeout report builders or renderers.

adversarial.desc: Prove the fix landed on the right line: run grep -n "never claims automatic DONE or production readiness" packages/main/src/core/command-policy.ts and assert it returns NO match (the pre-fix tail is gone), while grep -n "never claims automatic DONE, production, or remote Authority readiness" packages/main/src/core/command-policy.ts returns exactly one match on the milestone_status line — guards against editing the wrong line or a partial edit.

Guard against corrupting the adjacent milestone_closeout line: node -e "const {getCommandPolicy}=require('./packages/main/dist/core/command-policy.js'); const r=getCommandPolicy('milestone_closeout').reason; if(!/remote Authority readiness/.test(r)) throw new Error('milestone_closeout Authority disclaimer regressed: '+r); console.log('milestone_closeout intact');" — exits 0, confirming the neighboring closeout reason was not corrupted by the edit.

items.title: Add negative-control test: duplicate ledger rows are de-duplicated or rejected by the ledger builder
items.context: packages/main/src/tasks/proofstory-intent-hardening-smoke.ts has zero duplicat* coverage (grep = 0 hits, the withdrawn M5 claim). Add an assertion that milestone_ledger_set/buildMilestoneLedger with two rows sharing an id is rejected or de-duplicated. Closes findings M5 test-gap #1.
items.userSees: Running `node dist/tasks/proofstory-intent-hardening-smoke.js` (or the wired `npm test` entry that includes it) prints `ProofStory intent hardening smoke passed` and exits 0, now with new negative-control assertions exercised. If the ledger builder ever stops de-duplicating, the run instead fails with an assertion like `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: milestone_ledger_set with two rows sharing an id M1 is rejected` and a nonzero exit. Concretely, invoking `lattice milestone_ledger_set '{"storyId":"B-proofstory","milestones":[{"id":"M1",...},{"id":"M1",...}]}'` (two rows sharing id M1) exits nonzero and prints `duplicate milestone id: M1`; the same duplicate id fed to `milestone_ledger_add` (adding an id already present) exits nonzero and prints `duplicate milestone id: M1`, and neither call writes a corrupted milestone-ledger.json.

happy.desc: In proofstory-intent-hardening-smoke.ts add an assertion that `run(root, 'milestone_ledger_set', { storyId, milestones: [rowM1, rowM1dup] }, true)` (two normalized rows both with id 'M1') matches /duplicate milestone id/i, then build and run `node dist/tasks/proofstory-intent-hardening-smoke.js` and confirm it prints 'ProofStory intent hardening smoke passed' and exits 0.

Unit-assert against the pure builder: `buildMilestoneLedger({ storyId:'B-x', milestones:[{id:'M1',sourceRequirementId:'REQ-001',claim:'c',doneMeans:'d'},{id:'M1',sourceRequirementId:'REQ-001',claim:'c2',doneMeans:'d2'}] })` throws an Error whose message contains 'duplicate milestone id: M1' (matches the throw at proofstory.ts:330).

edge.desc: Add an assertion that `run(root, 'milestone_ledger_add', { storyId, milestone: rowWithExistingId }, true)` — appending a milestone whose id already exists in the persisted ledger (e.g. 'M1' after milestone_ledger_set wrote M1..M5) — matches /duplicate milestone id/i, exercising the addMilestoneToLedger de-dup path (proofstory.ts:358-360) distinctly from the set path.

Assert that after the rejected duplicate `milestone_ledger_set`/`milestone_ledger_add` calls, `jsonRun(root, 'milestone_ledger_get', { storyId })` still returns the prior valid ledger (milestones.length unchanged, no duplicate id present), proving the failed write did not corrupt or partially persist milestone-ledger.json.

adversarial.desc: Logic check that de-dup is by exact id and not silently coalesced: `buildMilestoneLedger` with two rows sharing id 'M1' but differing claim/doneMeans throws (rejected) rather than merging into a single row or keeping the last-writer — confirm the error is raised BEFORE computeMilestoneLedgerHash so no ledger object with length 1 is ever returned for a 2-row duplicate input.

CLI adversarial: run `node dist/tasks/proofstory-intent-hardening-smoke.js`; temporarily neutralize the duplicate guard in proofstory.ts (comment out the `if (ids.has(milestone.id)) throw` block) and confirm the newly added negative-control assertion FAILS with a nonzero exit (the test is un-gameable / actually detects a regressed builder), then restore the guard and confirm the suite passes again.

items.title: Add negative-control test: empty / all-not_applicable confirmed ledger is not treated as vacuously complete
items.context: core/proofstory.ts uncovered-required-milestone loop (~L1357-1364) iterates only ledger.milestones; a confirmed ledger with an empty or all-not_applicable milestone set yields zero uncovered rows. Add a test proving a confirmed-but-vacuous ledger does NOT satisfy the milestone DONE requirement. Closes findings M5 test-gap #2 and M4 caveat.
items.userSees: Running the milestone DONE-equivalence suite (`npm --prefix packages/main run build && node packages/main/tests/milestone-status.test.mjs`) prints a new passing assertion block such as `ok - negative control: confirmed empty ledger is NOT vacuously milestone-complete` and `ok - negative control: confirmed all-not_applicable ledger is NOT vacuously milestone-complete`. Concretely, when `evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence` is called in `enforce` mode with a `state: 'confirmed'` ledger whose `milestones` array is empty (and again with a ledger whose every row is `status: 'not_applicable'`), on the strict-milestone path (forced by a structural multi-deliverable story signal / slicePlan), the returned report has `status: 'fail'` and `blocking: true`, and `report.gaps` contains a gap whose `code` flags the vacuous/empty required-milestone set (e.g. `vacuous_milestone_ledger` / `uncovered_required_milestones`) with severity `fail` — instead of the pre-fix behavior where `uncoveredRequiredMilestoneIds` is `[]` and the report silently returns `status: 'pass'`. An operator who reaches DONE with such a ledger sees the DONE gate refuse to close the story, citing that a confirmed milestone ledger with no applicable required milestones does not satisfy strict intent equivalence.

happy.desc: In packages/main/tests/milestone-status.test.mjs, import evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence from dist/core/proofstory.js and call it in 'enforce' mode with a story whose text carries a structural multi-deliverable signal (e.g. 'all milestones') plus a confirmed ledger built via ledger([]) (empty milestones). Assert the returned report has status==='fail', blocking===true, and report.gaps contains at least one gap with severity 'fail' referencing milestone-ledger.json whose code marks the required-milestone set as empty/vacuous. Verified by: npm --prefix packages/main run build && node packages/main/tests/milestone-status.test.mjs exits 0 with the new assertions passing.

Second negative-control case in the same test: call evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence('enforce') with a confirmed ledger of one or more rows where every row has status 'not_applicable' (via milestone({status:'not_applicable'})). Assert the report is status==='fail'/blocking===true with the same vacuous-ledger gap, proving the all-not_applicable ledger is not treated as complete even though the uncovered loop 'continue's every row.

edge.desc: Positive-control guard against over-triggering: in the same test, call evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence('enforce') with a confirmed ledger containing at least one applicable (status!=='not_applicable') milestone whose verificationIntentRefs are all covered by passing verificationEvidence in the checklist. Assert the report status==='pass' and gaps contains NO vacuous/uncovered_required_milestones gap — confirming the new negative-control guard fires only for the vacuous set, not for a genuinely-satisfied ledger.

Boundary case: a confirmed ledger with exactly one applicable milestone plus one not_applicable milestone, applicable one covered — assert the vacuous guard does NOT fire (report status 'pass'), proving 'vacuous' is defined as 'zero applicable/required rows remaining' and a single applicable row is enough to escape the negative control.

adversarial.desc: Vacuity-via-accepted-shrinkage attack: build a confirmed ledger with applicable milestones but supply a confirmed+userConfirmed scopeShrinkageDecision that marks every applicable milestone id as accepted shrinkage, so acceptedShrinkage.has(...) 'continue's all rows and uncoveredRequiredMilestoneIds ends up empty. Assert this does NOT let the story pass vacuously — either the shrinkage-covered-everything case still yields a fail/warn gap or is explicitly distinguished from the empty/all-not_applicable case the guard targets (documenting intended behavior so the fix cannot be bypassed by shrinking away 100% of milestones).

Regression sweep: run the full pre-existing milestone-status suite (node packages/main/tests/milestone-status.test.mjs) after adding the guard/test to confirm zero prior assertions break — in particular the existing markerLedger DONE-coverage cases and the ledger([], 'B-closeout-empty') closeout-snapshot case that legitimately uses an empty ledger on the read-only status path (not the DONE-equivalence path), proving the new negative control does not mis-fire on the read-only milestone_status report.

verificationEvidence.note: Added a minimal contract-preserving empty_confirmed_milestone_ledger guard in evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence plus negative-control tests: empty confirmed ledger fails (enforce blocks), all-not_applicable-without-decision fails via not_applicable_missing_decision, and a positive control confirms the guards do not over-fire on a genuinely-covered ledger. Un-gameability verified by neutralizing the guard in dist and observing the empty-ledger assertion fail.

items.title: Add negative-control test: a stale-only status report is rejected by buildMilestoneCloseoutSnapshot
items.context: packages/main/tests/milestone-status.test.mjs stale-evidence block (~L749-870, stale ledger built ~L823) only asserts milestone_status demotes the row; no test feeds a stale-only report into buildMilestoneCloseoutSnapshot to assert it throws. Add that closeout negative control. Closes findings M5 test-gap #3.
items.userSees: Running `npm --prefix packages/main run build && node packages/main/tests/milestone-status.test.mjs` completes with a `# stale-only closeout negative control passed` style success (process exit 0, no `AssertionError`). The newly added assertion block inside the stale-evidence section (~L806-868) proves that the same stale-only `report` which `milestone_status` demotes to the `Current` group also causes `buildMilestoneCloseoutSnapshot({ report })` to THROW. The operator sees the run reach the end of the suite ("all milestone-status assertions passed") only because the closeout guard rejected the stale report with a message matching `incomplete milestone rows: M-stale=current`. If someone regresses the guard so a stale-only report is silently frozen into a closeout snapshot, this run instead fails with `AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Missing expected exception` (the `assert.throws` firing), naming this negative control.

happy.desc: In the stale-evidence block of packages/main/tests/milestone-status.test.mjs (after the existing L849-868 assertions that confirm `report.groups.completed === []` and `report.groups.current === ['M-stale']`), add `assert.throws(() => buildMilestoneCloseoutSnapshot({ report }), /incomplete milestone rows: M-stale=current/, 'stale-only report must be rejected by closeout snapshot')`. Then run `npm --prefix packages/main run build && node packages/main/tests/milestone-status.test.mjs`; it exits 0, proving the stale-only report both demotes M-stale to Current AND is refused by buildMilestoneCloseoutSnapshot.

edge.desc: Confirm the closeout guard fires on the FIRST-failing gate for a stale row: assert the thrown Error message begins with `Cannot create milestone closeout snapshot for` and contains `incomplete milestone rows: M-stale=current` (the status!=='completed' check at milestone-status.ts L885-891 runs before the risk check at L893-899), documenting that demotion-to-current, not merely the stale risk, is what blocks closeout. Verify via the same `node packages/main/tests/milestone-status.test.mjs` run passing.

adversarial.desc: Mutation check that the test is un-gameable: temporarily edit milestone-status.ts L885-891 to drop the `incomplete` guard (e.g. force `incomplete = []`), rebuild with `npm --prefix packages/main run build`, and run `node packages/main/tests/milestone-status.test.mjs`; the new negative control must now FAIL with `AssertionError ... Missing expected exception` (the stale-only report would otherwise be frozen into a closeout snapshot). Revert the mutation and confirm the suite passes again, proving the assertion actually catches a regressed guard rather than passing vacuously.

verificationEvidence.note: Added stale-only negative control: buildMilestoneCloseoutSnapshot throws on a report whose only defect is stale milestone evidence, and the DONE-time capture wrapper degrades that same report to a non-throwing skip with no write.

items.title: Wire packages/main/tests/milestone-status.test.mjs into an aggregate suite runner so it is not silently skipped
items.context: run-all-smokes.ts discoverSmokes globs dist/tasks/*-smoke.js; the .mjs test under packages/main/tests/ is named by no test:* npm script and its header documents manual invocation. Add a test:* script and/or run-all-smokes inclusion so it runs in the aggregate suite. Closes findings M5 suite-wiring gap.
items.userSees: Running `npm run test:milestone-status` from the repo root prints the milestone-status regression's terminal output ending in `ok milestone-status` and exits 0. Running the aggregate suite `npm test` from the repo root now includes a `> proofbound@... test:milestone-status` step in its &&-chain whose output shows `ok milestone-status`; if that .mjs regression fails, `npm test` aborts with a non-zero exit at that step (the milestone-status test is no longer silently skipped by the aggregate suite). `npm run` lists a `test:milestone-status` entry, so the test is named by a discoverable script. The head comment of packages/main/tests/milestone-status.test.mjs no longer documents only manual invocation — it names the `npm run test:milestone-status` / `npm test` wiring.

happy.desc: From repo root run `npm run test:milestone-status`; assert exit code 0 and stdout contains `ok milestone-status`. Confirms the named root script runs the milestone-status .mjs regression to completion against the prebuilt dist.

Run `node -e "const s=require('./package.json').scripts; if(!s['test:milestone-status']) process.exit(2); if(!s.test.includes('npm run test:milestone-status')) process.exit(3);"`; assert exit 0. Confirms a `test:milestone-status` root script exists AND the aggregate `npm test` &&-chain references it via `npm run test:milestone-status`.

edge.desc: Assert the two-hop delegation chain: `node -e` reads package.json and requires root `test:milestone-status` === `npm --prefix packages/main run test:milestone-status`, then `execFileSync('npm',['--prefix','packages/main','run','test:milestone-status'])` output contains `ok milestone-status`. Confirms the root script does not run node directly but delegates through the packages/main workspace script, and the delegated leg runs green.

Assert the deliberate no-inline-build design via `node -e`: packages/main `test:milestone-status` === `node tests/milestone-status.test.mjs` (relative invocation, contains no `build` step because dist is prebuilt by the separate top-level `build` chain step), and packages/main/tests/milestone-status.test.mjs resolves its imports from `new URL('../dist/', import.meta.url)`. Confirms the test loads compiled code relative to itself rather than rebuilding inline.

adversarial.desc: Simulate a regression: temporarily insert `assert.fail('injected')` right after the imports in packages/main/tests/milestone-status.test.mjs, then run the milestone-status chain leg inside `sh -c 'npm run test:milestone-status && touch MARKER'`; confirm the leg exits non-zero, `ok milestone-status` is absent, and MARKER is never created (the &&-chain aborts at this step so the next aggregate step never runs). Revert to a byte-identical file afterward. Proves the test is genuinely gate-observable in the aggregate suite and cannot be silently skipped.

Confirm the wiring does NOT depend on run-all-smokes discovery: assert `discoverSmokes` in both packages/main/src/tasks/run-all-smokes.ts and its compiled packages/main/dist/tasks/run-all-smokes.js still filters `endsWith('-smoke.js')` unchanged, so a `tests/*.test.mjs` file is invisible to discovery and the milestone-status regression runs only because of the named npm script/chain, not a discovery-glob change that could accidentally pull in every tests/*.mjs.

items.title: Gate not_applicable milestone rows behind an explicit justification so they cannot be a zero-evidence self-exemption
items.context: core/proofstory.ts normalizeMilestone (~L301-316) validates not_applicable against VALID_MILESTONE_STATUSES only, with no rule that the row is genuinely inapplicable; it then short-circuits the uncovered-required check and renders in the completed group. Add a required justification/reason field (or policy) for not_applicable, without weakening the PLAN-only, hash-bound, intent-collision-confirmed write contract. Design-decision item; record the decision. Closes findings M4 caveat.
items.userSees:
When an operator runs `milestone_ledger_add` (or `buildMilestoneLedger`) with `status=not_applicable` but no justification, the CLI now fails instead of silently accepting the row. Terminal shows a shape error like:

  Error: milestones[2].notApplicableDecision is required when status is not_applicable (needs reason, decidedBy, decidedAt)

When the justification is supplied (e.g. `--not-applicable-reason "REQ-014 covered by parent story P-9; no runtime behavior here" --decided-by info@retiave.com`), the add succeeds and `milestone_ledger_get --json` shows the row carrying `"notApplicableDecision": { "reason": "...", "decidedBy": "...", "decidedAt": "2026-07-05T..." }`. That justification is folded into `ledgerHash`, so editing the reason on a previously `confirmed` ledger drops its state back to `candidate` (visible as `State: candidate` on the next add and loss of `acceptedIntentBinding`). The DONE-intent-equivalence gate still skips the row from `uncoveredRequiredMilestoneIds`, but only because the row now carries a validated, hash-bound, human-attributed reason — an unjustified `not_applicable` row can no longer reach a confirmed ledger and therefore can no longer self-exempt from the uncovered-required check. The decision is recorded at docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-not-applicable-justification.md.

happy.desc: Logic: buildMilestoneLedger with a milestone {status:'not_applicable', notApplicableDecision:{reason:'covered by parent P-9', decidedBy:'info@retiave.com', decidedAt:'2026-07-05T00:00:00Z'}} returns a ledger whose row round-trips the notApplicableDecision object unchanged (assert deep-equal on ledger.milestones[0].notApplicableDecision).

CLI: against a scratch git+story fixture run `node packages/main/dist/cli.js --root <root> milestone_ledger_add {storyId, id:'M-na', ..., status:'not_applicable', json:true}` with NO decision flags and assert exit 0, the added row is persisted with status='not_applicable' and NO notApplicableDecision key (the write path deliberately does not reject an undecided row — the CLI surface has no decision flags), and `milestone_ledger_get --json` confirms the same persisted shape; then `done_intent_equivalence_check {mode:'observe', json:true}` over that CLI-written row emits a not_applicable_missing_decision gap naming M-na and status is not 'pass'.

Logic: for a not_applicable row that carries a valid notApplicableDecision, evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence omits that milestone id from uncoveredRequiredMilestoneIds AND emits no not_applicable_missing_decision gap for it (assert the id is NOT in uncoveredRequiredMilestoneIds and no gap.code==='not_applicable_missing_decision').

edge.desc: Logic: normalizeMilestone via buildMilestoneLedger with status='not_applicable' and a notApplicableDecision present but reason='' (empty) throws an Error whose message names milestones[i].notApplicableDecision.reason and says 'non-empty' (present-but-malformed shapes are rejected structurally at normalize time).

Logic: a non-not_applicable row (status 'planned'|'covered'|'done') builds successfully with notApplicableDecision omitted (assert the field is undefined), and a notApplicableDecision supplied on a 'done' row does NOT throw and round-trips unchanged (the field is status-independent and never rejected for non-exempt statuses).

Logic: changing a not_applicable row's notApplicableDecision.reason changes computeMilestoneLedgerHash (assert hash before != hash after), and rebuilding a previously-confirmed ledger (existing.state='confirmed') with the changed reason demotes it to state 'candidate' with acceptedIntentBinding cleared to undefined.

adversarial.desc: Logic (self-exemption attack blocked at the gate): a milestone with status='not_applicable' and NO notApplicableDecision is written by buildMilestoneLedger with the field absent (write path does not throw — deliberate hash-stable design), but evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence over the confirmed ledger emits a not_applicable_missing_decision gap of severity 'fail' naming the row and its status is not 'pass' — so a zero-evidence not_applicable row cannot self-exempt (the closed M4 caveat is enforced by the DONE gate, not a normalize throw).

Logic (gate cannot consume an unjustified exemption): construct a CONFIRMED milestone ledger whose only row is not_applicable without a decision; assert evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence in 'enforce' mode returns blocking=true, status='fail', and a not_applicable_missing_decision gap — and that the SAME shape carrying a valid notApplicableDecision does NOT raise that gap (proving the gate keys on the presence of an auditable decision, not merely the not_applicable status).

Logic (contract not weakened + hash-bound): decidedAt supplied as a whitespace-only string is rejected the same as empty (assert buildMilestoneLedger throws an Error naming milestones[i].notApplicableDecision.decidedAt and 'non-empty', since requireNonEmptyString trims), and a valid not_applicable row's notApplicableDecision is inside the sha256 ledger-hash input so it is hash-bound (assert computeMilestoneLedgerHash of the row WITH the decision differs from the SAME row with the field removed).

items.title: Re-assert confirmedLedgerHash === ledgerHash inside confirmMilestoneLedger at confirm time
items.context: core/proofstory.ts confirmMilestoneLedger (~L382-402) mints state=confirmed from an accepted intent collision without re-checking collision.confirmedLedgerHash === ledger.ledgerHash; today safety is emergent (any later row change routes through set/add which reset to candidate). Add an explicit confirm-time hash re-check so the invariant is local. Closes findings M2 hardening note.
items.userSees: Running the milestone-ledger confirm flow, the operator sees confirmation minted only when the accepted intent-collision was decided against the exact current ledger. Concretely: `node dist/tasks/proofstory-intent-hardening-smoke.js` prints `proofstory-intent-hardening-smoke: PASS` including the new assertion `confirmMilestoneLedger re-checks collision.confirmedLedgerHash === ledgerHash at confirm time`. In the CLI, `intent_collision_set --decision pass` against an unchanged ledger still returns `confirmedLedger.state = "confirmed"` (unchanged happy path), and `proofstory_gate_check` still reports `ledgerState: "confirmed"`. But if the ledger rows drifted after the collision was accepted (its `confirmedLedgerHash` no longer equals the current `ledgerHash`), `confirmMilestoneLedger` now returns the ledger still in `state: "candidate"` instead of falsely minting `confirmed` — the invariant is enforced locally at confirm time rather than relying on downstream set/add resets.

happy.desc: Logic: call confirmMilestoneLedger(storyId, ledger, collision) where collision is an accepted pass collision (collisionAccepted true, acceptedInterpretationHash set) whose confirmedLedgerHash === ledger.ledgerHash (computeMilestoneLedgerHash over the current milestones); assert the returned ledger has state==='confirmed', ledgerHash unchanged, acceptedIntentBinding.intentCollisionId === collision.id AND acceptedIntentBinding.acceptedInterpretationHash === collision.acceptedInterpretationHash — proving the added confirm-time re-check does not regress the normal matching-hash confirm path.

CLI/integration: in proofstory-intent-hardening-smoke.ts, intent_collision_set with decision 'pass' immediately after milestone_ledger_set (no intervening row change) yields passCollision.confirmedLedger.state === 'confirmed' (smoke L464) and a subsequent proofstory_gate_check reports ledgerState === 'confirmed' (smoke L467); running node packages/main/dist/tasks/proofstory-intent-hardening-smoke.js exits 0 and prints 'ProofStory intent hardening smoke passed', proving the happy confirm path holds end-to-end through the CLI.

edge.desc: Logic: build a ledger and mint an accepted pass collision recording its confirmedLedgerHash, then MUTATE the ledger (add a milestone so computeMilestoneLedgerHash differs) and call confirmMilestoneLedger with the STALE collision; assert the returned ledger stays state==='candidate' (not 'confirmed') and acceptedIntentBinding is undefined — proving the confirm-time re-check at proofstory.ts:455 catches ledger drift.

Logic (matches the ACTUAL fail-open design, not the over-specific old intent): call confirmMilestoneLedger with an accepted collision whose acceptedInterpretationHash is set but confirmedLedgerHash === undefined (older-schema). Assert it DOES mint state==='confirmed' against the current ledger, because the drift guard `if (collision.confirmedLedgerHash && collision.confirmedLedgerHash !== ledgerHash)` only fires when a recorded hash EXISTS and MISMATCHES — an absent recorded hash has nothing to contradict the current ledger. Also assert that the same collision with a recorded-but-DIFFERENT confirmedLedgerHash returns state==='candidate', proving the guard distinguishes undefined (no recorded decision) from a genuine mismatch.

adversarial.desc: Logic (guard + acceptance still required beyond the hash check): pass a null ledger with a fully-accepted collision and assert confirmMilestoneLedger returns null and never throws (guard clause preserved). Then pass a non-accepted collision (decision 'revise_intent', status 'open') carrying a MATCHING confirmedLedgerHash and assert the ledger is returned unchanged in state==='candidate' with no acceptedIntentBinding — acceptance is still mandatory in addition to the hash check. Finally pass an accepted collision with acceptedInterpretationHash===undefined and assert it does NOT confirm (state 'candidate'), proving both acceptance predicates guard the mint.

Integration/CLI: run the full proofstory-intent-hardening-smoke.js end to end via node packages/main/dist/tasks/proofstory-intent-hardening-smoke.js after npm --prefix packages/main run build; assert exit code 0 and the 'ProofStory intent hardening smoke passed' output, confirming the confirm-time invariant coexists with the whole gate/ledger/collision flow and no downstream diagnostic (confirmedLedger.state 'confirmed', gate ledgerState 'confirmed', missingIntentCollision length 0) regressed.

Decide (with a recorded rationale/decision-doc) whether milestone-triggered stories should default to enforce; observe->enforce is a behavior change with wide blast radius, so this is a decision item, not a blind flip. Closes findings M3/M7 gate-mode default question.

items.title: Reconcile the milestone_status vs DONE-gate stale-evidence disagreement and the closeout second-gate divergence
items.context: B-b550 M7 follow-up item 4 (the completeness-critic's two MAJOR holes). (1) milestone_status demotes stale milestone evidence (row -> groups.current, statusDetail=stale), but evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence (packages/main/src/handlers/phase-gates.ts; milestone coverage resolved via evidenceCoversIntent) can still pass the SAME stale ledger — the two surfaces give contradictory verdicts on identical stale evidence. (2) captureMilestoneCloseoutSnapshotFromStore (packages/main/src/handlers/milestone-status.ts, invoked from the DONE transition in transition-orchestrator.ts, phase==='DONE') acts as an undesigned second DONE gate with divergent throw semantics vs the designed evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence gate: a legitimately shrunk / non-applicable-but-risky confirmed ledger makes the designed gate pass while the closeout builder throws, blocking DONE. Reconcile so (a) milestone_status freshness and the DONE gate agree on stale milestone evidence, and (b) closeout capture is not a divergent second gate — with a recorded decision + tests. Design-decision + code; closes findings M7 follow-up item 4.
items.userSees:
Two concrete, observable changes plus a recorded decision doc.

(a) Stale-evidence agreement. With a milestone-triggered story whose confirmed ledger's required verificationIntentRef has a PASS evidence row bound to an OLD headHash/materialHash (git HEAD has since advanced), the operator now sees BOTH surfaces agree:
- `lattice milestone_status --storyId=B-<id>` still demotes the row out of Completed into Current with `statusDetail` containing `evidence=stale` and a risk like `Verification intent <ref> has stale passing ... evidence ...`.
- `lattice story_advance --storyId=B-<id> --phase=DONE` under `doneGateMode: enforce` now ALSO fails the DONE intent-equivalence gate with:
  `Cannot enter DONE: ProofStory intent equivalence gate did not pass` and a gap line `uncovered_required_milestones ... Required milestone(s) lack passing verification evidence ...` listing that milestone id (previously this gate PASSED on the same stale ledger — the contradiction is gone). Re-running the evidence against the current binding clears both.

(b) Closeout no longer a divergent second DONE gate. For a confirmed ledger that legitimately passes the designed gate but whose milestone_status report is incomplete/risky (e.g. a row removed by a user-confirmed scope_shrinkage_decision, or a risky `not_applicable` row), the operator now sees DONE COMPLETE:
- `✓ milestone closeout snapshot captured for B-<id>` (or a non-blocking `ℹ milestone closeout captured with caveats: <reason>` line) instead of the transition aborting.
- The transition no longer throws `Cannot create milestone closeout snapshot for B-<id>: ... incomplete milestone rows` / `... milestone report has risks:` AFTER the designed gate already passed. The single DONE verdict is owned by `evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence`; the closeout step is a recorder that never blocks DONE.

A decision doc at docs/requirements/decisions/milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md records: which surface is authoritative on stale milestone evidence (the shared freshness predicate, made freshness-aware on the gate side to match milestone_status), and that milestone closeout capture is a non-gating recorder subordinate to the designed DONE gate.

happy.desc: Fresh-evidence agreement: build a confirmed milestone ledger whose single required verificationIntentRef has a PASS evidence row bound to the CURRENT headHash/materialHash/storyFilesHash; assert buildMilestoneStatusReport places the row in groups.completed (statusDetail has evidence=covered) AND evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence(input, 'enforce') returns status='pass' with uncoveredRequiredMilestoneIds empty — both surfaces agree the row is covered.

Closeout records a complete-and-clean report without throwing: feed a report whose milestones are all status='completed' with zero risks into the reconciled captureMilestoneCloseoutSnapshotFromStore path and assert it returns {status:'written'} and store.writeMilestoneCloseout was called (no throw) — the recorder still captures the normal DONE case.

End-to-end DONE on a clean milestone-triggered story via the CLI (node packages/main/tests/milestone-status.test.mjs after npm --prefix packages/main run build) still prints '✓ milestone closeout snapshot captured' and reaches phase DONE, proving the reconciliation did not regress the passing path.

edge.desc: Stale-evidence disagreement is eliminated: same confirmed ledger as the happy case but the PASS evidence row's headHash/materialHash are the OLD hashes while the current binding is a NEW head; assert milestone_status demotes the row to groups.current with statusDetail containing 'evidence=stale' AND evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence(input,'enforce') now returns blocking status='fail' with a gap code 'uncovered_required_milestones' naming that milestone id (asserts the previously-contradictory gate no longer passes stale evidence).

Scope-shrunk row does not make closeout throw: confirmed ledger with a required row removed by a user-confirmed scope_shrinkage_decision so evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence passes but the milestone_status report marks that row current/incomplete; assert the reconciled closeout capture returns a non-throwing result (written or skipped-with-caveat) rather than throwing 'incomplete milestone rows', and that DONE completes.

Permanent-waiver parity: a required intent covered only by a permanent non-failing waiver bound to the CURRENT binding is treated as covered by BOTH evidenceIsCovering (milestone_status) and the freshness-aware gate coverage check (evidenceCanCover-style waiver acceptance is preserved, not broken by the new freshness gate).

Empty storyFilesHash / head-only binding: when the current binding carries only a headHash (no materialHash/storyFilesHash), a PASS row whose headHash matches by the >=7-char prefix rule is covered on both surfaces, and a mismatched headHash is stale on both — asserts the gate reuses the exact evidenceFreshnessRisks prefix/empty-hash semantics milestone_status uses.

adversarial.desc: Risky not_applicable row cannot silently block a legitimately-passing DONE via the closeout throw: confirmed ledger with a status='not_applicable' row that still carries a risk; assert evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence passes (not_applicable rows are skipped) and the reconciled closeout capture does NOT throw 'milestone report has risks' to abort the transition after the designed gate already passed — DONE is not blocked by the undesigned second gate.

Closeout cannot fabricate a DONE verdict either: with stale-only covering evidence (so the freshness-aware gate FAILS in enforce mode), assert the DONE transition aborts at the designed gate (runLegacyReceiptTransitionGate throws 'Cannot enter DONE') BEFORE writeStory/actor.send-persisted DONE and before captureMilestoneCloseoutSnapshotFromStore runs — i.e. reconciliation moved the block to the designed gate and did not weaken it into a pass.

CLI negative control that both surfaces agree on stale evidence end-to-end: drive a story to a DONE-ready state, advance HEAD so the recorded milestone evidence goes stale, then run `lattice milestone_status` (must show evidence=stale) and `lattice story_advance --phase=DONE` under enforce (must fail with uncovered_required_milestones) in the same fixture — proving the two CLIs no longer render contradictory verdicts on identical stale evidence.
